today_summary: GCM26 marked $4,652.6, down $41.2 (-0.88%) — the first clean down session of the week and 0.57σ against the $72.10 implied daily move. The notable change is beneath the headline P/C OI of 0.37: inside the ±25% strike window put OI jumped 56,434 → 64,174 (+7,740, +13.7%) in a single session while calls added only 1,890, lifting window P/C from 0.495 to 0.554. Net GEX within ±$200 of spot is +494.8 and effectively unchanged on the week, so dealers remain long gamma and the pin is intact. First shelf below is $4,600 (4,793 call OI), then the $4,500/$4,510 block holding a combined 16,002 call contracts — the structural floor and the gamma flip.
five_day_thesis: The five-day picture has turned from accumulation into distribution without breaking structure: spot is +$82.1 (+1.80%) from $4,570.5 on 08-21, but it peaked at $4,697.1 on 08-25 and has given back $44.5 over the two sessions since. What actually changed this week is the hedging mix. Window P/C OI compressed 0.570 → 0.494 through 08-25 as buyers chased calls, then reversed hard to 0.554 on 08-27 — the entire swing came from a downside ladder built in one session at $4,550 (+273 puts), $4,300 (+222), $4,200 (+229) and $4,400 (+153). Implied vol did not confirm the fear: ATM IV is +1.45pp on the week (23.15% → 24.60%) but fell 0.53pp on the down day itself, which reads as orderly de-risking rather than a bid for protection. Participation continues to drain — call volume 12,610 → 20,417 → 7,438 → 6,897 → 4,888 and put volume 3,651 → 2,108 — so the put build is positioning, not flow. Through all of it the gamma flip has not moved off $4,510 for five straight sessions and net GEX at spot has held between +401.9 and +503.1, meaning the dealer regime that pinned the tape last week is still the one governing it now.

prediction: Base case remains a pinned, slowly decaying range: +494.8 net GEX at spot, a five-session IV that has outrun realized movement, and 4,888 contracts of call volume are not the ingredients of a directional leg. The new put ladder tilts the near-term bias mildly lower toward the $4,600 shelf, but downside is structurally capped at $4,500/$4,510 where 16,002 call contracts sit long-gamma; only a sustained break below $4,510 turns cumulative GEX negative and opens the thin corridor to $4,300 (2,618 put OI). The bullish case needs a reclaim of $4,700 (3,749 call OI) on volume that has been absent all week. Treat max pain $6,000 as skew from legacy far-OTM call OI (18,112 at $6,000, 27,026 at $8,000), not a reachable target.
